reference.title: ESP32-S31-WROOM-3 & WROOM-3U Datasheet; IO MUX from ESP32-S31 Series Datasheet v0.5

pins.name: EN
pins.note: Chip CHIP_PU. High: chip on; low: off. Do not leave floating; RC delay 10k/1uF recommended (p63).

pins.name: IO2
pins.note: IO MUX F0 and F1 both GPIO2 (Table 2-3). LP_* entries are LP IO MUX codes (Table 2-5).

pins.name: IO3
pins.note: IO MUX F0 and F1 both GPIO3. LP_* entries are LP IO MUX codes (Table 2-5).

pins.name: IO0
pins.note: IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO0; LP IO MUX F0/F1 both LP_GPIO0. XTAL_32K_N is analog F0 (Table 2-7).

pins.name: IO1
pins.note: IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO1; LP IO MUX F0/F1 both LP_GPIO1. XTAL_32K_P is analog F0 (Table 2-7).

pins.name: IO4
pins.note: IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO4. DAC_CH0 from Table 2-8 / Sec 4.2.3.4 (no mux code given).

pins.name: IO5
pins.note: IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO5. DAC_CH1 from Table 2-8 / Sec 4.2.3.4 (no mux code given).

pins.name: IO6
pins.note: IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO6. TOUCH_CH0 analog F0.

pins.name: IO7
pins.note: IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO7. TOUCH_CH1 analog F0.

pins.name: SD_D0
pins.note: Powered by internal VDDPST_SD domain (VDDPST_2 or VDD_LDO_1P8).

pins.name: USB_DP
pins.note: USB 2.0 High-Speed OTG PHY D+ (chip pin 44, dedicated; Table 2-9).

pins.name: USB_DM
pins.note: USB 2.0 High-Speed OTG PHY D- (chip pin 45, dedicated; Table 2-9).

pins.name: IO33
pins.note: Default: USB Serial/JTAG D- (analog F0, bold). IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO33.

pins.name: IO34
pins.note: Default: USB Serial/JTAG D+ (analog F0, bold). IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO34.

pins.name: IO36
pins.note: Strapping pin (VDD_SPI voltage). Pulled up inside the module (R10 10k, Table 3-1 note 2 / Fig 8-1) = 3.3 V flash. IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO36.

pins.name: IO37
pins.note: Strapping pin (JTAG signal source). IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO37.

pins.name: IO60
pins.note: Strapping pin (boot mode, UART0 ROM print); weak pull-up at reset. IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO60.

pins.name: IO61
pins.note: Strapping pin (boot mode); weak pull-up at reset. IO MUX F0/F1 both GPIO61.

pins.name: NC
pins.note: NC on WROOM-3 (ANT2 on WROOM-3U). Leave unconnected.

pins.name: GND
pins.note: EPAD: 9-pad diamond ground array, one terminal. Soldering optional, improves thermal performance (p63).

rules.label: strap_gpio36_vdd_spi
rules.script: if pin_used("45") { warn("Pin 45 (IO36/GPIO36) is a strapping pin sampled at reset: VDD_SPI voltage (with EFUSE_PMU_FLASH_POWER_SEL=0, default). Chip default floating; the module pulls it up (R10) = 1 -> 3.3 V for the module's 3.3 V flash. Holding it low at reset selects 1.8 V.") }

rules.label: strap_gpio37_jtag_source
rules.script: if pin_used("46") { warn("Pin 46 (IO37/GPIO37) is a strapping pin: JTAG signal source when EFUSE_JTAG_SEL_ENABLE=1 (1 = USB Serial/JTAG, 0 = JTAG pins). Default floating, no internal pull; ignored with default eFuses. If the eFuse is set, drive it to a defined level at reset.") }

rules.label: strap_gpio60_boot_print
rules.script: if pin_used("70") { warn("Pin 70 (IO60/GPIO60) is a strapping pin, default weak pull-up = 1. With GPIO61=0 it selects Joint Download Boot (needs GPIO60=1; GPIO60=GPIO61=0 is invalid); it also controls UART0 ROM printing when EFUSE_UART_PRINT_CONTROL is 1 or 2. Keep it high at reset.") }

rules.label: strap_gpio61_boot_mode
rules.script: if pin_used("71") { warn("Pin 71 (IO61/GPIO61) is a strapping pin, default weak pull-up = 1 = SPI Boot. 0 (with GPIO60=1) = Joint Download Boot. Never hold GPIO61 and GPIO60 both low at reset (invalid, unexpected behaviour).") }

rules.label: jtag_pins_reuse
rules.script: for p in ["64", "65", "66", "67"] { if pin_used(p) && !function_used(p, "MTDO") && !function_used(p, "MTCK") && !function_used(p, "MTDI") && !function_used(p, "MTMS") { warn("Pins 64-67 (IO54-IO57) carry pad JTAG MTDO/MTCK/MTDI/MTMS; using them otherwise loses pad JTAG (use USB Serial/JTAG on IO33/IO34 instead).") } }

rules.label: usb_serial_jtag_reconfigure
rules.script: for p in ["42", "43"] { if function_used(p, "GPIO33") || function_used(p, "GPIO34") || function_used(p, "LCD_DATA12_OUT_PAD") || function_used(p, "LCD_DATA13_OUT_PAD") { warn("Pins 42/43 (IO33/IO34) are connected to the USB Serial/JTAG controller at reset (USB pull-up enabled); firmware must disable USB Serial/JTAG before using them as GPIO, and USB download/debug is lost.") } }

rules.label: uart0_console_reuse
rules.script: if function_used("68", "GPIO58") || function_used("69", "GPIO59") { warn("Pins 68/69 (TX0/RX0) are UART0, used for ROM messages and UART download; reusing them as GPIO affects the boot console and download.") }

rules.label: lp_uart_flow_vs_lp_i2c
rules.script: if (function_used("10", "LP_UART_RTSN_PAD") || function_used("11", "LP_UART_CTSN_PAD")) && (function_used("12", "LP_I2C_SCL_PAD") || function_used("13", "LP_I2C_SDA_PAD")) { forbid("LP UART hardware flow control and LP I2C cannot be used at the same time (chip DS Table 2-5 note 2).") }

open_questions: Is the 0.7 mm dimension (Fig 10-1/11-1) to the pad centre (as built) or the pad outer edge? Also confirm 20.6/22.6 are centre-to-centre.
Ground array: confirm pitch 2.35 mm (derived), pad 1.8 mm and the meaning of the two '1.3' dimensions (possibly a chamfer on the top diamond, Fig 3-1); thermal vias are shown but not dimensioned.
Side rows assumed vertically/horizontally symmetric between corner pads; the drawing does not dimension the end gaps directly.
Pin-rule Rhai API is undocumented in the schema: scripts use guessed pin_used()/function_used()/warn()/forbid() and must be verified/rewritten before relying on them.
Mux code collision: LP IO MUX and analog functions reuse F0–F3 names; confirm the tool disambiguates by peripheral or rename (e.g. 'LP F0').
Antenna keep-out on the host board is not dimensioned in this datasheet (refers to Hardware Design Guidelines); keep-out currently equals the 6 mm antenna region only.
PCB thickness 1.0 mm read from side view; not explicitly labelled.
Both datasheets are PRELIMINARY (v0.7 / v0.5); chip DS v0.5 predates module DS v0.7 — recheck IO MUX tables against the latest chip datasheet.
Flash/PSRAM pins (SPICS..SPID, GPIO26–32) are not brought out on the module, so no forbid rule was needed; confirm no module pin connects to them.
Design-default function for IO9–IO19 was set to the bold SPI2_* F0 entry; reviewer may prefer GPIO as symbol default.
report.part: ESP32-S31-WROOM-3 (Espressif module, ESP32-S31NRVxx inside; 99-terminal LGA, PCB antenna)
report.summary: Built: component/symbol (draft 1/2) from an imported pinout of 99 rows (94 edge pads 1–94, ground array EPAD 95 as one terminal, corner ground pads 96–99); package draft 3 + footprint draft 5 + binding 4 + generated 3D model from the custom module form; text marking 'ESP32-S31-WROOM-3' + pin-1 dot. All drafts check publishable; 99 imported rows are unreviewed (review gate). Check first: (1) the 0.7 mm edge-to-row dimension (Fig 10-1/11-1) — read as module edge to pad CENTRE; if it is to the pad outer edge every row moves 0.4 mm inward; (2) ground-array interpretation (pad 1.8, gap 0.55, span 6.5 ⇒ pitch 2.35, 45°, centred at (0,−3)) and the unexplained '1.3' dimensions; (3) the pin-rule scripts: the schema documents no Rhai API, so the scripts call guessed functions pin_used(number), function_used(number,label), warn(), forbid(); they compile but were never evaluated — they may fail at run time and must be rewritten against the real API; (4) mux codes: IO MUX, LP IO MUX and analog tables all number from F0, so e.g. 'F0' on IO2 can mean LP IO MUX F0 (LP_UART_DTRN) while IO MUX F0 is GPIO2 — the peripheral field disambiguates (LP_* = LP IO MUX, TOUCH/ADC/XTAL_32K/USB_SERIAL_JTAG/ANALOG_COMPARATOR = analog F0). Where IO MUX F0 and F1 are both GPIOn only one GPIO function (mux F1) is listed (stated in pin notes). Frame: module datasheet drawings are dimensioned symmetric; top-view numbering from Fig 3-1 (top view) was used, no bottom-view mirroring needed. Derived positions (module frame, origin outline centre, antenna +y): left row x=−10.3, pins 1..25 y=7.2…−13.2; bottom row y=−14.3, pins 26..47 x=−8.925…8.925; right row x=10.3, 48..72 y=−13.2…7.2; top row y=8.3, 73..94 x=8.925…−8.925; corner pads 96(−10.3,−14.3) 97(10.3,−14.3) 98(10.3,8.3) 99(−10.3,8.3); verified in the built footprint (107 pads, 99 terminals).

report.part: ESP32-S31-WROOM-3 (Espressif module, ESP32-S31NRVxx inside; 99-terminal LGA, PCB antenna)
report.summary: Built: component/symbol (draft 1/2) from an imported pinout of 99 rows (94 edge pads 1–94, ground array EPAD 95 as one terminal, corner ground pads 96–99); package draft 3 + footprint draft 5 + binding 4 + generated 3D model from the custom module form; text marking 'ESP32-S31-WROOM-3' + pin-1 dot. All drafts check publishable; 99 imported rows are unreviewed (review gate). Check first: (1) the 0.7 mm edge-to-row dimension (Fig 10-1/11-1) — read as module edge to pad CENTRE; if it is to the pad outer edge every row moves 0.4 mm inward; (2) ground-array interpretation (pad 1.8, gap 0.55, span 6.5 ⇒ pitch 2.35, 45°, centred at (0,−3)) and the unexplained '1.3' dimensions; (3) the pin-rule scripts: the schema documents no Rhai API, so the scripts call guessed functions pin_used(number), function_used(number,label), warn(), forbid(); they compile but were never evaluated — they may fail at run time and must be rewritten against the real API; (4) mux codes: IO MUX, LP IO MUX and analog tables all number from F0, so e.g. 'F0' on IO2 can mean LP IO MUX F0 (LP_UART_DTRN) while IO MUX F0 is GPIO2 — the peripheral field disambiguates (LP_* = LP IO MUX, TOUCH/ADC/XTAL_32K/USB_SERIAL_JTAG/ANALOG_COMPARATOR = analog F0). Where IO MUX F0 and F1 are both GPIOn only one GPIO function (mux F1) is listed (stated in pin notes). Frame: module datasheet drawings are dimensioned symmetric; top-view numbering from Fig 3-1 (top view) was used, no bottom-view mirroring needed. Derived positions (module frame, origin outline centre, antenna +y): left row x=−10.3, pins 1..25 y=7.2…−13.2; bottom row y=−14.3, pins 26..47 x=−8.925…8.925; right row x=10.3, 48..72 y=−13.2…7.2; top row y=8.3, 73..94 x=8.925…−8.925; corner pads 96(−10.3,−14.3) 97(10.3,−14.3) 98(10.3,8.3) 99(−10.3,8.3); verified in the built footprint (107 pads, 99 terminals).
